PART III  Nutrition in the Life Cycle
•	 Development of social, emotional, financial, and physical 
independence from family as teens leave home to attend 
college or seek employment
•	 Development of a core set of values and beliefs that 
guides moral, ethical, and health decisions
The psychosocial development of adolescents has a direct 
bearing on the foods and beverages they choose. Food choices 
are more likely to be based on taste, cost, and peer behaviors 
than on health benefits because these influences satisfy a teen’s 
innate preference for immediate reward. Nutrition education 
and counseling methods that focus on how adolescents look, 
such as improving skin appearance or promoting hair growth, 
are most likely to be effective with young teens because these 
reinforce emotional influences.
